In the mentioned pages, the fortune teller doesn't tell Hassan's fortune because his future is already sealed. The fortune teller is unwilling to reveal Hassan's tragic destiny. 

Amir pulls his hand back because he is nervous about knowing his future.

On page 73-74 of The Kite Runner, the fortune teller chooses not to tell Hassan his fortune due to noticing something unusual about Hassan's hand. Specifically, he sees that Hassan is missing the pinky finger of his right hand, although in the scene the fortune teller sees a birthmark that resembles a split. Amir pulls his hand back as he is anxious that the fortune teller may say something unfavorable about his future.

In the scene on page 73-74 of The Kite Runner, the fortune teller does not reveal Hassan's fortune because he saw something in Hassan's palm that made him uncomfortable or disturbed. He seemed to see a dark or ominous sign, and he chose to keep it to himself.

Amir pulls his hand back because he saw the fortune teller's reaction when reading Hassan's palm, and he became uneasy, feeling that something bad was going to be revealed. He was anxious about knowing his own future and decided not to take the risk.

On pages 73-74 of The Kite Runner, the fortune teller doesn't tell Hassan's fortune as he is somehow taken aback, uneasy, by what he sees when he takes Hassan's hand. This evokes an ominous, foreboding sense of dread.

As for Amir pulling his hand back, he gets frightened, anxious when the fortune teller takes his hand next. This fear stems from witnessing the fortune teller's intense, grim reaction to Hassan's hand.
